best_poem: Tiny hands reach out | Glowing dots dance in night air | Laughter sparks like stars
By the tracks the dusk draped its gray veil | He clasped a torn letter, his breath turned pale | No words left to speak | No tears left to leak | The engine’s sigh mourned the sorrowful rail
At twilight’s hush the whistle cries, | A soldier's kiss beneath grey skies, | His pulse now thin, | His thoughts within, | The train departs with whispered sighs.
Beneath waning light the platform did weep, | Grey smoke rose, a veil for the deep, | He folded his coat, | With a tremor of throat, | As the iron beast thundered, his promise to keep.
Dark lane, silent pulse | Footsteps mirror my own tread | Heart drums in the void
Empty street, cold fog | Footfalls sync, a silent drum | Panic claws my throat
Dark lane, heart pounding | A mirror stride behind me | Silence cracks like glass
Faded frame lies still | Edges curl like quiet tears | Forgotten drawer sighs
Paper curls like tears, | forgotten faces linger, | loneliness folds.

When thunder cracked the night, he fled, | He crawled beneath the bed, heart bled, | A whisper crept— | A clawed foot kept— | And eyes of darkness stared instead. | The storm roared loud while he did hide, | Under the mattress, trembling, wide, | A sigh, a growl— | His pulse did howl— | When something else was lying inside. | He shivered as the rain beat fast, | Beneath the springs his fear was cast, | A low, cold hiss— | A shadow’s kiss— | A beast that’d claimed the space at last. | The lightning flashed, the floorboards moaned, | He froze beneath the sheets, intoned, | A hiss, a grin— | His skin grew thin— | For something worse than storm had grown.
At twilight the whistle sighs soft and bleak | A soldier bends, his oath now torn and weak | Steam veils the night | His eyes lose the light | And the tracks hum onward with grief’s quiet streak
Beneath iron arches the shadows conspire, | He boards with a sigh, his eyes full of fire, | Will he see the sun? | The tracks hum, undone, | While sorrow drifts on the cold, mournful choir.
Steam curled like ghosts as the night grew dim, | He whispered his oath on a trembling limb, | The rails sang a moan, | His heart turned to stone, | And the station awoke to a mournful hymn.

At the station he lingers, his breath a thin thread, A | While the wind writes his name on the dead, A | The crowd turns to mist, | The night clenches its fist, | And the whistle cries out what words never said.
The rails sang low, a dirge of steel and rain, | A weary clasp let go, a silent pain, | The shadows fell, | His story’s knell, | Will daylight’s echo answer his refrain?
When thunder cracked the night and shook the floor, | He hid beneath the springs, his pulse a roar, | A shiver, a hiss— | A stare from abyss— | A phantom smiled, its teeth like jagged shore.
When thunder cracked loud through the night, | He slid beneath sheets, trembling with fright, | A soft rustle near, | A cold, hollow sneer, | And a pale hand clasped his wrist in the light.
A clumsy baker in wedding attire, | Set his tiered marvel to rise higher. | It tumbled, then sang, | A sweet, joyous clang, | Now guests cheer the crumble, their hearts on fire.
Bumbling baker, his whisk a wild kite, | Raised a cake that could out‑shine any light. | It toppled with cheer, | A sweet avalanche near, | And the guests ate the joy, every bite pure delight.
Morning gold spills bright | Tiny toes dance on soft grass | Hearts lift with the light
First light on the rise | Bare feet splash through silvered grass | Cheer blooms on the wind
Soft dew hugs each step | Hilltop glows with laughing eyes | Sun dances, carefree
Empty lane, breath held | Shadow steps echo my stride | Darkness leans closer
Street empties, eyes blind | Footfalls mirror trembling beat | Silence shatters now
Winter in a box | Photograph weeps at each seam | Drawer stays closed still
Memory’s thin skin | Edges curl, a quiet gasp | Drawer stays shut, cold
